Facebook Ad Scam UK: Check the Ad Library First

Meta's own Ad Library lets you check active ads across Meta apps and services — a genuine brand page should be checkable there.

By Alex Bacsa · Published 2026-05-04 · Updated 2026-07-10 · 4 min read

Facebook ad scam UKMeta Ad Library checkfake Facebook advertFacebook investment ad scamcounterfeit ad Facebooksocial media scam UK
Key rule: verify through an official route you opened yourself, not the link, number, app, or payment details supplied by the suspicious message.

Being targeted right now? Do this

  1. Stop. Don’t pay, transfer money, or share passwords, PINs, or one-time codes.
  2. Contact your bank on the number on the back of your card if your money or details may be at risk.
  3. Report it — call Report Fraud on 0300 123 2040 (Police Scotland: 101), and forward scam texts to 7726.

What the Facebook ad scam looks like

This scam is a paid advert on Facebook or Instagram using a real or near-identical brand's name and logo, promising something that doesn't hold up — a guaranteed investment return, heavily discounted branded goods, or a work-from-home job with unrealistic pay. An example of the style: LIMITED STOCK: [Brand] clearance sale, up to 80% off, today only — click to order. The ad often links to a professional-looking site or asks you to message a page directly, where the real request — a deposit, personal details, or upfront payment — follows.

Warning signs to look for

  • The brand name or logo is slightly different from the real company's, or the ad claims a discount far beyond what that retailer ever genuinely offers.
  • The advertiser's Facebook Page is new, has few followers, or its "About" details don't match the real company.
  • The ad promises guaranteed earnings or returns ("make £5,000 a week from home") with no clear, checkable explanation of how.
  • Clicking through leads to a site that only accepts bank transfer or an unusual payment method, not a normal checkout.
  • You're asked to message the Page directly and move the conversation to WhatsApp or email before completing any purchase.
  • The advertiser doesn't appear in Meta's public Ad Library, or appears there with different branding or claims to what you saw in your feed.

How this scam works step by step

A paid ad appears in your Facebook or Instagram feed, often looking identical to a genuine retailer or investment brand. Clicking through takes you to a site or a direct message conversation designed to extract payment or personal details quickly, before you have time to check further. If it's a goods scam, payment is taken and nothing arrives, or a cheap counterfeit turns up instead. If it's an investment or job scam, an initial payment or deposit is requested, followed by further requests once you've engaged, before contact stops entirely.

How to check an ad before you click

Search Meta's Ad Library (facebook.com/ads/library) for the advertiser's Page name. Meta describes it as a public tool for viewing active ads currently running across its apps and services; for social issues, election, or political ads, Meta provides additional transparency information. A Page with no active ads matching what you saw, or running ads inconsistent with the brand it claims to be, is a strong warning sign. Separately, go to the brand's official website directly — not through the ad's link — and compare prices, contact details, and offers. For further verification steps, see Is This Website a Scam? A Practical Checklist Before You Buy.

What to do if you've already paid

Contact your bank or card provider as soon as possible and explain what's happened — a card payment may be eligible for a chargeback if goods never arrive or are significantly not as described. Report the ad and the Page directly to Facebook or Instagram using the Report Ad or Report Page option. Keep screenshots of the ad, the Page, and any payment confirmation as evidence.

How to report a Facebook ad scam in the UK

Report the ad in-app using Report Ad, and report the Page itself. Report the scam to Report Fraud at reportfraud.police.uk or 0300 123 2040 if you're in England, Wales, or Northern Ireland — in Scotland, report to Police Scotland on 101. If you paid by card, ask your bank about a chargeback claim.

Frequently asked questions

How can I check if a Facebook ad is genuinely from the brand it claims to be?

Search Meta's Ad Library (facebook.com/ads/library) for the advertiser's Page. It shows active ads currently running across Meta apps and services; additional transparency details apply to social issues, election, or political ads. Also visit the brand's official website directly, not through the ad's link, and compare details.

Is Meta's Ad Library a real, current tool I can actually use?

Yes — it's Meta's own public transparency tool for active ads across Meta apps and services, with extra information for social issues, election, or political ads.

I paid for something advertised on Facebook and it never arrived — what now?

Contact your bank or card provider and ask about a chargeback claim, since a card payment for goods that never arrive is often eligible. Report the ad and the Page to Facebook using Report Ad, and report the scam to Report Fraud.

How do I report a scam Facebook ad?

Use Report Ad on the advert itself and report the Page separately. Report the scam to Report Fraud at reportfraud.police.uk or 0300 123 2040 (Police Scotland on 101 in Scotland).
